dedupe_keys.name: siasar rural water and sanitation information system communities water systems and service providers in 14 countries

description: SIASAR is a shared information system on rural water supply and sanitation services, started by the governments of Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama and extended to other countries. Field teams survey rural communities, water systems, the service providers that run them and the technical assistance providers with a mobile app; the data are edited and validated before entering the system, which classifies the state of each element with a set of indicators for monitoring coverage, quality and sustainability. The participating governments produce it, and on 2026-09-26 the SIASAR Data dashboard showed about 40,700 communities, 28,900 systems and 25,000 service providers. Coverage is 14 countries: Bolivia, Brazil (Ceará), Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Honduras, Kyrgyzstan, Mexico (Oaxaca), Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Uganda and Tanzania. Country data are a free download as zipped spreadsheets from SIASAR Data; the site says the information is public and free to use, and its content is under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Caveats: in Brazil and Mexico only one state takes part (Ceará, Oaxaca), and the Colombia file was last modified in June 2024. Simulation uses: rural water system inventories, their condition and their operators for planning rehabilitation and sustainability. Related record: the Water Point Data Exchange (data-wpdx-water-point-data-exchange).
